title: Divina Proportione (Italian, 1509)
author: Luca Pacioli
description: Divina Proportione (On the Divine Proportion) by the Franciscan mathematician Luca Pacioli, printed in Italian in Venice in 1509 with sixty illustrations of polyhedra drawn by his friend Leonardo da Vinci. The first part, the Compendium de divina proportione, studies the 'divine proportion' (the golden ratio, or extreme and mean ratio), listing its thirteen 'effects' and its theological significance as a proportion that, like God, is unique and cannot be expressed rationally, and applies it to the regular and semi-regular solids. Further sections treat architecture and the proportions of the human body after Vitruvius, the design of Roman capital letters, and an Italian translation of Piero della Francesca's work on the regular solids. A landmark of Renaissance mathematics and art theory, it gave the golden ratio its sacred name and underpins later sacred-geometry traditions.
